Batch: JoeWare W2KLockDesktop and WriteProt publisher source review

Scope.AdFindAcceptance: Excluded from selected acceptance batches; no AdFind action in this review.

Findings: Publisher describes W2KLockDesktop as a command-line tool that immediately locks the desktop.
The product page and versions list identify version 1.0.0 / 01.00.00 dated 2001-05-10; publisher states no local security requirement.
Published platform list is Windows 2000, Server 2003 and XP; this historical statement does not establish Windows 11 support.
Publisher describes WriteProt as a utility for changing fixed-volume write protection, version 1.0.0 dated 2004-08-08; local administrator rights are required to modify volume state.
Published platform page names Windows XP and Server 2003; this historical statement does not establish current Windows support.
Read-only observation switches include /view, /mview, /diskinfo, /volinfo and /info; /ro and /rw change a selected volume's state.
On a basic disk with multiple volumes, changing one volume may affect all volumes; /unsafe explicitly overrides the publisher's warning.
Publisher warns that making the system partition read-only can make a PC unusable.
W2KLockDesktop row: 01.00.00 dated 2001-05-10; publisher MD5 6ac3acb478d4c39cafa25610708e12bd and SHA-1 72108f7602363064adc32c7e6f7b0d63bb958db8.
WriteProt row: 01.00.00 dated 2004-08-08; publisher MD5 1410134ff602b0ea3719fbc52a02cfcd and SHA-1 253504025a3335bae43e14c9edea23b57b96b0cf.
Publisher digests are observations only; no archive was acquired and no local archive hash was verified.

Resolved: Publisher product purpose, offered version and documented behavior boundaries for two members of the frozen review scope.
Deferred: Exact archives, local SHA-256 hashes, signatures/notices and member inventories.
Bounded package lifecycle/recovery and current-target acceptance.
W2KLockDesktop interaction must be tested only in a disposable logged-in VM session.
WriteProt mutation must use a disposable VM with a dedicated secondary virtual disk; never test the system volume or a developer workstation.

Estimate.Adjustment: Unchanged; source review established behavior boundaries but no exact package artifact or Windows acceptance.
